title: Comparing and Ordering Numbers to 120
seo_title: Grade 1 Comparing and Ordering Numbers Worksheets (TEKS 1.2E)
standard_text: 1.2D generate a number that is greater than or less than a given whole number up to 120; 1.2E use place value to compare whole numbers up to 120 using comparative language; 1.2F order whole numbers up to 120 using place value and open number lines; 1.2G represent the comparison of two numbers to 100 using the symbols >, <, or =
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 worksheets for Texas TEKS 1.2D–1.2G: compare numbers to 120 with blocks and place value, use >, < and =, and order numbers. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Compare the tens first, then the ones.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Compare the tens first. More tens means a greater number.
  • If the tens are the same, compare the ones.
  • > means greater than, < means less than, = means equal to. The open side faces the greater number.
  • To order numbers, find the least, then the next, and so on.

Examples

Example

Compare 43 and 61

4 tens < 6 tens

Answer: 43 < 61

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Comparing the ones firstLook at the tens first.
Turning the symbol the wrong wayThe open side faces the greater number.
Reading 52 as 25Say the tens digit first.

sets.title: Compare with tens and ones blocks

items.q: What number does each group show? Which number is greater?
items.e: A has 4 tens and 4 ones: 44. B has 1 ten and 5 ones: 15. Look at the tens first. 44 has 4 tens and 15 has 1 ten. 4 tens is more than 1 ten, so 44 > 15. The ones do not matter. 44 is the greater number.
